question: does feeding HMcode the cold-matter spectrum plus the real f_nu improve m_nu = 0.30 eV?
setup: one cosmology (sum m_nu = 0.30 eV, f_nu = 0.02215), our own solver on a 32-point k grid over 1e-3..5 h/Mpc, two HMcode builds sharing the same linear solve
verdict: MIXED, not an improvement. The high-k end gets better - k = 4 goes 0.9483 -> 0.9667, i.e. the 5.2% deficit halves to 3.3%, which is the region where the f_nu factors in p_1h, dc_Mead and Dv_Mead actually act. But the mid and low end gets worse: k = 0.1 goes 1.0085 -> 1.0452, and k = 0.5, 1.0 both move up by 3-4pp. Net max|dev| 6.42% -> 6.30%, i.e. essentially unchanged.
a_second_and_more_important_finding: the absolute numbers here (6.4%) are far worse than the 1.40% measured earlier for the same cosmology, and the only difference is the k grid: this run fed HMcode 32 points, the earlier one fed it CAMB's 16384-point spectrum. So grid density dominates both candidates, and this comparison is compressed against a 6.4% floor - it cannot resolve which input is right.
what_that_implies: the cold-spectrum question is still open. To answer it, HMcode has to see a dense spectrum; on a 32-point grid the answer is swamped. That is consistent with the earlier finding that a 2-point grid gave 27% error at k = 1 where a dense one gave 0.86%.
status: cold_spectrum_change (commit 30afb7d) stays UNVERIFIED. It is not shown to help; at k = 4 it helps and at k <= 1 it hurts. Do not quote an improvement for it.
cost_note: this single-cosmology, 32-point comparison took 37 minutes of wall time at 99.7% CPU. The linear solve is ~1 min per trajectory on this machine.
